integrity: The claim is proved analytically from finite-dimensional spectral subspaces, tie-priority inequalities, and orthogonal-projection geometry; no numerical experiment is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The target-safe subspace is only sufficient and can be zero even when target-class states exist.
The certificate is vacuous when the encoded input has zero overlap with the target-safe subspace.
The result assumes the source model's pure inputs, unitary hidden evolution, exact known POVM, fixed tie priority, and access to derived binary projector readouts.
No equality with the optimal targeted robustness radius is claimed.
title: A target-safe spectral-intersection upper certificate under known-readout query access
